answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive at an admission oasis: every newcomer locks a jade collateral bond equal to the median established stake, then needs three sponsors who also escrow a slice of their own bond. If peer audits later prove the newcomer is a sockpuppet, both parties forfeit the jade. A willow of time-decaying sponsor vouchers further caps how many identities any one agent can midwife per epoch, so farms cannot outrun the collateral curve.
